newsitem.title: USA: California Micro says judge ok's settlement.
newsitem.headline: California Micro says judge ok's settlement.

text.p: California Micro Devices Corp said a U.S. District Court judge has approved a tentative settlement with the class representatives in pending securities class action lawsuits against the company and some of its former officers.

In a statement, the proposed approved settlement is intended to resolve all of those claims raised against the company and and all defendants other than Chan Desaigoudar, the company's former chairman and chief executive.

Under terms of the agreement, approved by U.S. District Court Judge Vaughn Walker, California Micro will pay to the class $6 million in cash and 608,696 shares of California Micro Devices common stock. Each share of common stock will be accompanied by a contingent value right, which will be personal to the class member, guaranteeing that the stock will trade at an average price of at least $11.50 per share, for 20 consecutive trading days within three years after issuance of the stock. Once that price is met, the contingent value right will expire.

In addition, California Micro will assign to the class its pending claims against Desaigoudar. The company will also assign to the class its rights under its directors and officers liability insurance policies, and will enter into a mutual release of all claims with Coopers & Lybrand, California Micro's former auditors. The value of the company's portion of the settlement, $13 million, is the same as that of a prior proposed settlement for which charges have already been taken. The company also noted other major litigation activities had been concluded in recent weeks, and that the elimination of both these and the class action lawsuits will reduce the company's legal expenses significantly.
